translit: Bismillāhir-Raḥmānir-Raḥīm. Al-ḥamdu lillāhi Rabbil-ʿālamīn. Wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa ʿalā ālihi wa ṣaḥbihi ajmaʿīn. Allāhumma ʿallimnā mā yanfaʿunā wa nfaʿnā bimā ʿallamtanā wa zidnā ʿilmā.

text: Rabbi shraḥ lī ṣadrī wa yassir lī amrī wa ḥlul ʿuqdatan min lisānī yafqahū qawlī.
Last week, when talking about the early childhood of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we talked about how he moved from household to household.
And this is the way of an orphan, that when the father dies and the mother dies, then they are moved from household to household. And this is what happened with the Prophet ﷺ.
So first, of course, for the first couple of years of his life, he was brought up in the desert with his wet nurse [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رضي الله عنها]].
And then she returned him to his mother after two years.
And he lived with his mother for another about four years, and then his mother died when [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ was about six years old.
So a six-year-old boy, he already lost his father even before he was born, and now he's only six years old and he lost his mother as well.
Very difficult childhood that [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ had to go through.
After that, he stayed with his grandfather, who was the leader of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the head of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
So he stayed with [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], his grandfather, for another two years.
So from the age of six to eight, he stayed with his grandfather [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
And then [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] also died.
So now the Prophet ﷺ, he is an eight-year-old young boy, and he has been brought up already in three households.

First in the household of [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رضي الله عنها]], then in the house of his own mother, [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]], and then in the care of his grandfather [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
And now, at the age of eight, when the Prophet ﷺ was eight years old, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] also passed away.
After this, the Prophet ﷺ went to live with his paternal uncle [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]].
[[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] was one of the most respected sons of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
And he was the brother of the father of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.

The father of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, as we mentioned, his name was [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], and [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] ibn [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] was his brother.
So he was the paternal uncle of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, and he took him to care for him after [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] died.
He took in his eight-year-old nephew, [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, and he treated him as if he was his own son.
He didn't treat him as an outsider, as a nephew. No, he treated him as his own son.
And he even used to call him, "[[ibni|ابني]], this is my son."
When people used to ask, "Who is this boy?" he would say, "This is my son."
So he had an immense love for this boy, and he treated him as if he was his own.
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ also grew very attached to [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]].
So they both loved each other, they both cared for each other, and they both respected each other very deeply.
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ stayed with [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] for a number of years.
When [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ was 12 years old, so he had been living with [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] now for about four years...
He came into his household when he was eight years old, now he's about 12 years old.
So during these four years, they bonded, they became very close, and they both loved each other deeply.
So one summer, when [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ was 12 years old, [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] was getting ready to make a business trip up to [[Sham|شام]].
[[Sham|شام]] is the Greater Syria area.
So he was getting ready one summer to make a trip up to [[Sham|شام]].
And it was well known that the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they used to take two major journeys every year: one journey in the summer and one journey in the winter.
In the summer, they would go up to [[Sham|شام]], the Greater Syria area, and do business there. And in the winter, they would go south to [[Yemen|اليمن]].
Because in the winter, [[Sham|شام]], it would be very, very freezing cold, so they wouldn't go there in the winter.
They would go to [[Yemen|اليمن]] in the winters, and they would go to [[Sham|شام]] in the summers. And Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala mentions this habit of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]]:
Li-ilafi Qurayshin. Ilafi-him rihlata ash-shitai was-sayf.

The [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] has become accustomed, this has become a habit of them, to make these two journeys: [[rihlat ash-shitai was-sayf|رحلة الشتاء والصيف]], the journey of the winter and the journey of the summer.
The journey of the winter was to [[Yemen|اليمن]], and the journey of the summer was to [[Sham|شام]].
So [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], he's getting ready for the summer journey to go up to [[Sham|شام]].
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ is about 12 years old at this time, young boy still.
But he asks his uncle to allow him to accompany him on this journey.
He was excited and he said, "Can I go with you?"
And [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], he doesn't think that this is a good idea, and he tries to convince him, "No, let me go, you stay here in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]."
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ starts to cry because he really wants it, he really wants to go with his uncle.
So he starts to cry, and he asks his uncle again and again, "Please let me go with you, uncle. Please let me go with you."
And the sons of [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] are witnessing this, [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ crying and asking [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] to let him accompany him on this journey.
So the sons of [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] tell [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, "Leave him, don't do this, just stay here with us, stay in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and let him go."
And [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] tells his sons, "No, don't worry about it, I will take him with me. I will take him with me."
So he tells his own sons to stop trying to tell [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ to stay, and he tells them that "I will take him, I will accompany him, I will let him accompany me on this journey."
So [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ is very happy and he's excited that he gets to go on this trip all the way to [[Sham|شام]].
And he has never actually left the greater [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] area since he came back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] from [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]]...

...since [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]], his wet nurse, brought him back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to live with his mother when he was two years old, since that time he had never been on a trip like this.
He had never been outside the greater [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] area.
So he's very excited to take this first big journey in his life, and he's going to go with his uncle.
So he's happy and he's excited, and the caravan leaves [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], going towards [[Sham|شام]].

And the caravan, of course, it has a number of people from the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], it's not just [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] and [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ. No, it's a lot of people, a group of people from the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] making that journey.
So they are moving on the way from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to [[Sham|شام]].
And on the way, on the pathway from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to [[Sham|شام]], they passed by a monastery, a Christian monastery.
And in this Christian monastery, there lived some monks.
They used to live in the monastery, and they used to devote all of their time in worship.
They used to detach themselves from the [[dunya|دُنْيَا]] completely, and they used to just spend all of their time in worship.
And this is not something that Allah prescribed them to do.
This is something that they started to do as a form of extremism in leaving the [[dunya|دُنْيَا]], but this is not the way that Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala commanded them or commanded us.

Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala says about this type of way of living, just spending all of your time in the house of worship, only worshipping and having nothing at all to do with this [[dunya|دُنْيَا]]...
Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala says about that way of life:
wa rahbaniyyatan ibtada'uha ma katabnaha 'alayhim

This is a way of life, this [[rahbaniyyah|رَهْبَانِيَّة]], this monk lifestyle of cutting off the [[dunya|دُنْيَا]] completely, this is something that they innovated, that those people, they invented. It is not something that was revealed to them by Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala.
[[ma katabnaha 'alayhim|مَا كَتَبْنَاهَا عَلَيْهِمْ]], "We did not prescribe this for them."

Anyhow, this was the way that these monks used to live. They stayed in the monastery and they used to just spend all of their time worshipping, and they cut themselves off completely from the [[dunya|دُنْيَا]].
And the head of these monks in this particular monastery that the caravan passed by, the head of these monks was a man named [[Buhayra|بحيرى]].
And he noticed the caravan coming close, and he noticed...
